target_customer: Online media buyers and sellers, ad networks and advertisers who pay to detect malware, click fraud and inappropriate content in ads
problem: Ads and ad placements could serve malware or be hit by click fraud, and advertisers had little visibility into where their ads ran.
business_model: B2B software subscription for ad verification and monitoring (pricing not verified)
product_category: Ad verification, click fraud and malvertising detection

founders.name: Mikhail Ledvich
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/Product Architect. No bio found.

founders.name: Mikhail Gurevich
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: an engineer trying to build cool stuff.

founders.name: Greg Gurevich
founders.background_notes: YC page lists expertise in machine learning, electronic trading and market microstructure.

competitors.name: Click Forensics
competitors.what: Click fraud auditing and reporting through its Click Fraud Network
competitors.traction_then: Published quarterly click fraud rate reports from 2006, disputed by Google

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting malware in SWF ads and tracking placements needed crawling, sandboxing and analytics, hard but doable for engineers with machine learning skills.

defensibility.rationale: Detection quality and historical ad placement data could accumulate, but several vendors sold similar audits and no switching costs are documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google contested click fraud vendors' figures in 2006. The acquirer of Clickfacts and the date are not public in sources found.

market_need_then: Click fraud was a widely covered concern in 2006, with one report of Google crediting an advertiser for clicks that Clickfacts flagged, and vendors reporting double digit fraud rates.

branding.domain_note: Company website field is empty in the directory; site appears dead or unknown.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, only product coverage.

pivots.to: Ad network publisher verification suite, later malware discovery and ad moderation
pivots.why: Product line expanded per MediaPost 2007 and the YC description; reasons not stated.

outcome_analysis: Clickfacts began in the 2005 YC batch selling click fraud detection into a loudly discussed 2006 market and later broadened to ad network verification, malware discovery and moderation. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or price turned up, so the exit quality and cause cannot be judged from public sources.
notes: Acquirer unknown. Aggregators (Employbl, Bouncewatch) report two debt financings of 232,708 and 615,000 dated 2010 (about 848K total); unverified aggregator figures, not recorded as rounds. CB Insights lists the company as alive, conflicting with YC status Acquired. Authenticlick was also named as a click fraud auditor in a search snippet. Company website is blank in the directory, so no site fetch was possible. Anchor Intelligence (2007 coverage) later entered click fraud auditing and is omitted from the founding list. No competitor source dated near the 2005 batch was found; the one listed is from late 2006. Completeness pass: the two 2010 debt financings are now recorded as rounds (Bouncewatch dates them 2010-03-04 and 2010-08-23; Employbl total 847,708 matches). They rest on aggregators only (Diffbot-derived data). CB Insights also lists an undisclosed YC seed dated 2005-06-13 (Seedtable/others say 2005-08), not recorded because no amount is given.
